sector: A heritage iron and bronze foundry casting bespoke architectural work for specifiers and developers.
founded_place_size: Casting since 1911 in the same Sheffield works; a small crew of founders, patternmakers and finishers.
about: Ironline Forge casts bespoke iron and bronze for architects and developers who have mostly never stood on a foundry floor. We sell permanence and provenance: the heat, the hands, and the fact that the piece will still be here in eighty years. The brand has to feel like the shop floor, hot, dirty and precise.
audience: Specifiers, architects and developers, 40 to 65, buying craft and confidence rather than a catalogue product.
price_positioning: Bespoke castings from five to sixty thousand dollars a piece, priced on provenance and never presented as a promotion.
typography: A generous editorial serif for headlines with plenty of black around it, and a strong grotesque for labels and spec lines. Numbers are set plainly.
voice: Plain, declarative, unshowy. Example line: 'Iron and bronze, cast in this building since 1911.'
brand_assets_status: Our maker's mark was cut into a die generations ago and survives only struck into the metal. There is no artwork for it anywhere, and the trade-fair stand and the brand story page are being rebuilt at the same time.
values: Process and provenance over polish. The struck maker's mark must be recovered faithfully rather than tidied into a fashion monoline, and it has to hold small and reversed out of the dark.
